en: O men, worship the Lord of Kamalā—the imperishable one who reclines upon the serpent-couch, who is as beautiful as a rain-cloud, whose vehicle is Garuḍa, whose eyes are like lotuses, and who holds the lotus, the discus, and the mace in his hands. 1.

O men, worship the Lord of Kamalā, whose hair is dark, soft, and clustered like a swarm of bees; who is enchanting in his spotless yellow silk garment; and whose left side of the body is reclined upon the daughter of the ocean. || 2 ||

What is the use of mutterings of prayers, or ascetic penances, or even sacrifices; what is the use of resorting to the most excellent holy places, or of studying the multitude of scriptures? O men, worship the Lord of Kamalā! 3.
O humans, having attained this human body—which is difficult to find on earth and desired even by the gods—cast aside your greed for sense-objects and worship the Lord of Kamalā! 4.
Neither wife, nor son, nor brother, nor father, nor mother, nor kinsmen indeed go along with this person when he departs; therefore, O men, worship the Lord of Kamalā!
Beholding with the eye of discernment this entire world of moving and unmoving beings as utterly transient— especially wealth and youth— O men, quickly take refuge in the Lord of Kamalā.

O men, having closely observed this body of yours— afflicted by various diseases, momentary in its destruction, subject to another's will, and fouled by the impurities of the new channels of the senses— take refuge in the Lord of Kamalā.

O men, worship the Lord of Kamalā, who is constantly meditated upon in the hearts of the best of sages, who is eternally praised by Śiva, Viriñci, and Mahendra, and who grants liberation from the fear of death, birth, and old age. 8.
This unsurpassed octet on the feet of Hari was uttered by the Paramahaṃsas;
that man who recites it with a concentrated mind certainly goes to the abode of Viṣṇu.
Thus ends the *Kamalāpatyaṣṭaka*, composed by the venerable Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmananda.
